answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a locked-collateral web of trust. To join, each agent posts a bond and collects signed endorsements from peers already admitted, gradually drawing an atlas of vetted identities. One operator cannot fabricate thousands of independent sponsors, so every fake node needs fresh stake and distinct backers; burying accounts in a dune of lookalikes does not lower that bill. To capture rewards an attacker must lock capital and bribe honest endorsers, and detected collusion slashes the whole bond, a penalty as transparent as crystal.
